To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ERAS protocol with oral feeding and the Bengmark protocol with nasojejunal feeding had similar 30-day complication and LOS rates, but that the rate of POI tended to be higher in the ERAS group, although not significantly.

the rate of postoperative complications and length of stay were similar in two cystectomy cohorts that differed in their postoperative feeding strategies, but that the rate of POI after cystectomy was significantly lower in patients who were fed via a nasojejunal feeding tube.
the use of a nasojejunal feeding tube is associated with a lower rate of POIs in patients undergoing cystectomy.

the comparison of two feeding strategies in an enhanced recovery after cystectomy (ERAS).
the comparison of the short-term outcome after cystectomies in patients with and without the use of a nasojejunal feeding tube.
the development of the Bengmark naso-jejunal tube.

the two protocols have comparable complication rates and LOS.
both protocols are equally safe and effective, and that the ERAS protocol is preferred because of its simplicity.
the ERAS protocol is superior with respect to the occurrence of POI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Bengmark-protocol is a safe, fast, and cost-effective alternative for the ERAS-protocol.
early oral feeding is feasible in a selected population of cystectomy patients.
early oral feeding is safe and may be considered in patients who are fit for oral nutrition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ERAS protocol is feasible and safe in patients undergoing cystectomy for bladder carcinoma.
early oral feeding in patients undergoing cystectomy is feasible and safe.
early feeding strategies in the perioperative setting should be tailored to individual patient needs.
